chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan, from Ibn Miskan, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He (peace be upon him) was asked about a newborn who was born with both a female organ (qubul) and a male organ (dhakar), how is it inherited? He (peace be upon him) said: If it urinates from its male part, then it has the inheritance of the male, and if it urinates from the female part, then it has the inheritance of the female.
ai.seo_question: How is inheritance determined for a hermaphrodite child in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the practical juristic method for determining the inheritance share of a hermaphrodite (mukhallat) by observing the primary site of urination, a criterion widely accepted in Shia fiqh. It reflects the scholarly approach of relying on observable physical signs to resolve ambiguity in inheritance distribution, ensuring fairness when gender is not definitively established at birth.
